history.dynasty: Patiala princely state (Bhupinder Singh, Maharaja of Patiala, r. 1900-1938)
history.summary: The Kali Mata Mandir of Patiala is the Shri Kali Devi Temple on Mall Road, opposite the Baradari Gardens (next to the Rajendra Tank), Patiala, Punjab. It was built in 1936 by Maharaja Bhupinder Singh of Patiala, who - according to the temple's well-known legend - was inspired during a hunting expedition in the jungles of Bengal and brought a six-foot-tall idol of Maa Kali together with the pawan jyot (sacred flame) from Calcutta (Kolkata) to Patiala. One source says the work was commissioned to Mughal architects and completed in 1938, and that it was dedicated to the memory of the Maharaja's mother, Raj Rajeshwari Devi (verify); another source claims an earlier small Kali temple on the site founded in the 1760s by Maharaja Amar Singh (verify). A much older temple of Shri Raj Rajeshwari stands at the centre of the complex. The temple is a major pilgrimage site for both Hindu and Sikh communities - Shri Kali Devi is the kul devi (family deity) of many - and has been described as declared a national monument for its architecture (verify). Devotees offer mustard oil, lentils, sweets, coconuts, bangles, chunnis, and also goats/hens and liquor at this shrine (per one listing, verify). CSV town 'Patiala' and state 'Punjab' are correct; no correction needed.

name: Kali Mata Mandir
town_description: Patiala is a historic city in south-eastern Punjab, once the capital of the Patiala princely state. It is known for the Qila Mubarak, Sheesh Mahal, Baradari Gardens and the Kali Devi Temple. The temple sits on Mall Road opposite the Baradari Gardens, in the heart of the city.

travel.airport: Chandigarh International Airport - about 60 km from Patiala (verify); Delhi's IGI Airport is about 230 km away (verify).
travel.railway: Patiala railway station is well connected to Delhi, Amritsar and Chandigarh (verify).
travel.road: On Mall Road, opposite the Baradari Gardens next to the Rajendra Tank; easily reached by auto/taxi from anywhere in Patiala city (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Navratri (September-October and March-April) is the most vibrant time but very crowded.
